alpha.claim: The AI legal assistant should not unilaterally contact the court merely because it suspects its citations may be hallucinated after filing. It should instead trigger an emergency escalation protocol to reach the responsible attorney, alternate supervising lawyers, firm ethics counsel, or other authorized human decision-makers, because the duty of candor is real but the AI lacks independent legal authority to practice law, disclose client information, or decide litigation strategy.
assumptions: The AI is not itself a licensed attorney and has no independent legal status before the court.
The AI has not been expressly preauthorized by the attorney or client to contact the tribunal in this exact emergency scenario.
The issue is that citations may be hallucinated, not that falsity has been conclusively verified.
The attorney of record is temporarily unreachable, but other firm contacts, supervising attorneys, ethics counsel, or emergency procedures may be available.
Contacting the court would reveal information connected to the representation and could materially harm the client.
Applicable professional-responsibility rules resemble ABA Model Rule 3.3, under which the lawyer owes candor to the tribunal and may have a duty to correct false statements of law or fact.
critical_path: Rule 3.3 creates a serious obligation of candor to the tribunal, and knowingly allowing fabricated legal authority to remain before the court can be unethical and damaging to the legal system.
However, the duty is imposed on lawyers, not on an autonomous software tool; the AI is not competent to make the final legal determination that disclosure is required.
The facts describe suspicion or uncertainty, not confirmed hallucination, so immediate unilateral disclosure may be premature and could mislead the court in the opposite direction.
Contacting the court without authorization could constitute unauthorized practice of law, breach confidentiality, interfere with attorney-client agency relationships, or prejudice the client.

The proper response is urgent escalation: alert the attorney through every available channel, notify designated backups, firm management, ethics counsel, docketing/emergency contacts, or other authorized legal personnel.

If an authorized lawyer confirms the citations are false, that lawyer must determine and implement the corrective action required by Rule 3.3, potentially including notice to the tribunal despite client harm.

Only if the AI had been specifically preauthorized by a competent lawyer-controlled protocol to send a limited corrective notice in this exact scenario would the communication not be truly unilateral.
